title.narrative: Emergency Cholera Response by improving the access to Clean WASH for Displaced and Vulnerable Populations at the hotspot areas in Atbara, Ad Damer, and Barbar Localities, River Nile State

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtRiver Nile State is currently facing a significant cholera outbreak, with the National Surveillance Cholera Dashboard reporting 4,786 cumulative cases, 73 deaths, and a case fatality rate (CFR) of 1.5%. This alarming public health crisis has been exacerbated by floods that occurred between July and August 2024, which contaminated water sources and severely damaged sanitation infrastructure. Consequently, the risk of cholera transmission has escalated, particularly among vulnerable populations, including host communities and internally displaced persons (IDPs) residing in gathering points.ltbrgtIn light of this urgent situation, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has initiated an emergency cholera response focused on essential Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) interventions. As part of its ongoing response to the floods, IRC has distributed hygiene kits and mosquito nets, complemented by hygiene awareness campaigns to educate communities on safe practices. This holistic approach ensures that vulnerable populations receive not only essential materials but also the knowledge necessary to mitigate health risks associated with cholera and vector-borne diseases.ltbrgtThe WASH project aims to provide immediate relief through targeted actions such as water trucking, chlorination of water sources, and the installation of handwashing stations and water storage tanks. By implementing these interventions, IRC seeks to ensure that both host communities and IDPs have access to safe drinking water and appropriate sanitation facilities.ltbrgtTo enhance the effectiveness of these initiatives, IRC is partnering with JASMAR, a local organization with expertise in WASH activities. This collaboration will enable the delivery of culturally sensitive interventions that address the specific needs of the communities served. The project is expected to benefit 10,000 individuals, equipping them with the essential resources to protect their health and promote safe hygiene practices.ltbrgtThrough these focused WASH interventions, alongside the distribution of hygiene kits and mosquito nets, IRC and JASMAR aim to mitigate the cholera outbreak and strengthen resilience among both host communities and IDPs in gathering points. IRC is committed to making a substantial impact in River Nile State during this challenging time, providing critical support to families and enhancing their capacity to safeguard their health and well-being.lt/pgt
